On [blog.interlis.guru][post], Stefan Ziegler is describing his experiment with 
a binary flavour of INTERLIS 2[^interlis] for data exchange, called "INTERLIS Binary 
eXchange" or "IBX" for short. From Stefan's post:

> [...] INTERLIS/XTF[^xtf] does have its advantages, but it is certainly not a 
user-friendly "working format". Users simply want to drag and drop the file into 
QGIS and be done with it. [...] Besides, the world keeps moving on, doesn’t it? 
Where is Cloud Native[^cloud-native] INTERLIS? [...] 
> 
> This fits perfectly with the basic concept of MDX[^mdx]. It explicitly states 
that encoding rules can, in principle, be defined for any data format. So why 
not a binary encoding that preserves the INTERLIS content whilst also enabling 
direct, selective access? That’s exactly where my experiment comes in: IBX – 
INTERLIS Binary eXchange.

In his experiment, Stefan built a prototype that supports INTERLIS 2.3 and 2.4 
full (not yet: update) data transfers. Stefan covers the details in his 
[post][post] and also provides both a [QGIS plug-in][plugin] (zip) to read IBX 
files and a [patched version of ili2db][ili2db] to write IBX files from 
GeoPackage[^geopackage] and PostgreSQL for testing purposes.

[post]: https://blog.interlis.guru/2026/09/28/interlis-leicht-gemacht-number-69/
[plugin]: https://blog.interlis.guru/2026/09/28/ibx-qgis-0.6.0.zip
[ili2db]: https://github.com/edigonzales/ili2db/releases/tag/ibx-2-1

[^interlis]: [INTERLIS](https://www.interlis.ch/en) is a Swiss standard for geodata modelling and data exchange.
[^xtf]: Interlis transfer format.
[^cloud-native]: I.e., taking full advantage of the cloud computing model; in the data world typically through enabling partial downloads of file contents through so-called [HTTP range requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Range_requests).
[^mdx]: Model-compliant data exchange.
[^geopackage]: An open SQLite-based container format for geospatial data, defined by the [OGC](https://www.ogc.org/).
